body.en: Jack, the narrator, grows up in America with an American father and a Chinese mother who came to the country after the father chose her from a catalogue. She folds *paper* animals that magically come alive, among them a little tiger, Laohu, and they are his treasured childhood companions. As Jack grows older, teased for being different, he becomes ashamed of his mother, refuses to speak Chinese and rejects her and her paper animals. She dies of cancer when he is in college. Years later, on the festival when the dead are remembered, a paper animal unfolds to reveal a letter in Chinese telling the story of her hard life and her love for him; Jack has it translated and finally understands what he has lost. Read the prescribed text itself; this guide is in our own words and quotes nothing.

text.en: Exposition
Young Jack and his mother; paper animals
that breathe and play; a happy home.
Rising action
Neighbours' taunts; Jack begins to feel
ashamed of his mother and her language.
Climax
He rejects her completely, and she stops
folding; the animals lie still.
Falling action
She falls ill and dies; Jack is
distant even at the end.
Resolution
Her letter in Chinese is found and
translated; Jack finally understands.

body.en: Adolph Knipe, an engineer who has failed as a writer, realises that English grammar follows rules almost as strict as mathematics. With his employer, Mr Bohlen, he builds a huge machine that writes stories and novels to order, adjusting style and length. Soon they produce vast numbers of works, and buy up famous authors' names, paying writers to stop writing and let the machine publish under their names. Most writers give in. The narrator, a writer, reveals at the end that he too is tempted, as his children are hungry, and he prays for the strength to refuse. The story is a dark satire of commercial publishing and of art produced by machines. Read the prescribed text itself; this guide is in our own words and quotes nothing.

problem.en: Is Jack a sympathetic narrator? Give two reasons for and one against.

steps.en: For: he was a child under real pressure from racist neighbours and classmates, which explains his shame.
For: he tells the story with honesty and deep regret, judging himself harshly.
Against: he is cruel to his loving mother, even when she is dying, and the reader feels her pain.
Conclusion: he is flawed but understandable, which makes the ending more moving.

answer.en: Yes, largely: his cruelty is real, but his honesty and regret earn sympathy.

heading.en: Paper is fragile; machines are not

body.en: The paper animals are fragile, handmade and full of love. The Grammatizator is huge, mechanical and loveless. Together they ask what makes something truly human.
